items.title: Annie Ross — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Tadd and I would just hang out. He would teach me things. I hung on his every word

ctx.x: Anyway, I met Tadd and his brother. Tadd and I would just hang out. He would teach me things. I hung on his every word, because anybody that has ears that big deserves – necessity – to expound, should be listen to. I was there, listening. He used to cook, and I used to cook. I think we spent a lot of time at the Alvin Hilton, which is what we all called it. Yeah, the Alvin Hilton. You’d come in there at night. It was across from Birdland. You’d go in at night. You’d see certain doors that were barricaded, because…
I’m trying to think of his – the guy – I don’t know.
